component.name: Backspace
component.summary: Self-hosted text, voice, and video communication

description.p: Backspace is a client for self-hosted Backspace communities. Connect to an instance to chat in spaces and direct messages, make voice and video calls, share your screen, and communicate with users on federated instances.
The desktop client adds native notifications, a system tray, deep links, and global push-to-talk keybinds where supported by the desktop environment.

screenshot.caption: Text channels with replies, reactions, and typing indicators
Voice and video calls with screen sharing

description.p: Backspace is now available in Brazilian Portuguese. Spaces and channels have notification settings: every message, mentions only or nothing, with a mute for a set time, and the bell in the channel header opens them. In a group conversation, a call keeps running when one member hangs up, and a member who calls while a call is running joins it. Channel topics can be edited and read in full, a reaction counts once per person, and a reply no longer follows you into another conversation.

Instances now catch up with each other regularly, so a direct message, friend or profile change that got lost between two instances arrives later instead of staying missing. Channels open at your first unread message, and the message list keeps your place while messages load and while the message box grows. People from different instances are no longer mixed up, and mentions and notifications on another instance's channels now recognise you. Roles can be dragged by their row again, and role changes no longer reset the open chat. Instance admins can see why a peer was rejected or needs attention.

Fixes changes between instances that could get lost or arrive out of order, such as a status change, an edit or a deleted message. A screen share now stays running for the sharer when the stream changes codec or the voice connection restarts, and the sharer hears when people start and stop watching, also across instances. The stream settings in the desktop app now say whether System Audio will include Backspace's own voice chat. On mobile, direct messages get a call button. The web app also downloads less at startup and moves to a new version after a hard reload.

Adds a role hierarchy with a way to order roles, lets moderators edit a member's roles from their profile card, and reworks how direct messages between instances are matched, so a conversation shows once however it was started. Also a setting to hide the floating call window.

Fixes conversations and friendships between instances: direct messages no longer show up twice, people from other instances are shown by their name from the first message, mentions and game activity work across instances, and two security issues in how users from other instances are recorded are closed.

Fixes two security issues in how an instance accepts events from the instances it is connected to, and a round of follow-ups to 1.6.0: quieter notifications, screen sharing that survives a codec change, a faster start, and fixes for connections between instances.

Replies jump to the message they answer, reactions show who reacted, channels can be renamed, Do Not Disturb silences notifications, and a round of fixes for direct messages and screen sharing between instances.

The Coming Soon item in the direct messages sidebar is now a Backspace page with the release notes, bug reports, feature requests, the install guide and a link to support the project on Ko-fi. Connecting to an instance with closed federated registration no longer says an account already exists there.

The instance setting that allows spaces in the global directory is now called Allow global listing, and it says that each space is still listed from its own Discovery settings. While nothing is listed, a note under it links to a space's Discovery settings.

Spaces on other instances are findable now. The Explore page has an Outer Space section listing spaces from instances you have never connected to, and joining one connects you to its instance first. Listing is opt in on both sides: the instance admin allows it and the space owner asks for it. Explore also names the instances that did not answer instead of quietly showing a short list.

Backspace has a new logo, on the app and every icon. The interface is available in Chinese, and Chinese and Russian text no longer split across two fonts. App Settings has a Desktop tab in the browser that offers the desktop download for your platform.

Screen sharing starts with a preview and quality controls before you go live. Fullscreen streams use the whole window, with the header and call controls fading out once the pointer stops moving, and a voice call now survives a reconnect instead of dropping what you had.
Adds a 50% step to the interface scale and keeps narrow windows on the mobile layout at any scale. Instance admins are now told in the app when a newer Backspace release is out.
Moves the language and interface scale settings out of Account into a new Appearance tab.
Adds an interface scale from 75% to 250%, opt-in instance telemetry, and voice shortcuts on Wayland. A system-audio screen share no longer plays viewers their own voice back.
Fixes the Register and Log In links on the login and registration pages, localizes the elapsed time under activities, and adds editing your last message with the up arrow.
Rebuilds the container image that failed to build for 1.1.0. No changes to the app beyond the version number.

Backspace now speaks English, Russian and German. Pick your language under Settings, Account; dates, numbers and server errors follow the choice. The Flatpak build can also use the webcam and talk to the system power service, so video calls work and the app can keep the system awake during a call.
First release with Flatpak packaging. In the Flatpak build, updates are handled by Flatpak rather than by the app, and the in-app update controls are hidden accordingly.
Reliable desktop update handling and maintenance improvements.
Security and maintenance improvements.
Security scanning improvements and Linux packaging fixes.
Security hardening and desktop packaging improvements.
Maintenance and reliability improvements.
First public release of Backspace.
